meta.title: Cherut — Structured obsession for the life you are building
meta.description: Turn ambition into one direction, daily execution, and a system that survives the hard days. Choose the system your direction requires.

hero.headlinePre: The only thing that distorts time is
hero.note: Choose the level of structure your direction requires.

pattern.heading: You know what to do. You still don't keep the promises you make to yourself.
pattern.lede: That gap is what wears down your trust in your own word. Cherut builds the structure that gets you out of the loop.
nodes: You hit tiredness, fear, boredom, or a distraction
quotes: I know what I need to do, but I keep doing something else.
I'm always starting a new version of myself.
I have potential, but my life doesn't show it.
I don't trust my own word anymore.
I'm tired of restarting, but I still haven't quit.
pattern.footPre: This isn't about discipline or laziness.

method.heading: Your obsession is not the problem. It has no structure.
method.lede: Cherut concentrates your energy and connects your values, objectives and daily actions. Fall off, and you can review and pick back up without starting over.

pillars.title: One Direction
pillars.body: Choose the one direction that matters most right now, not everything at once.

pillars.title: Structured Intensity
pillars.body: Turn intensity into actions, schedules and systems instead of short bursts.

pillars.title: Stay Through the Hard Moment
pillars.body: Move through boredom, fear and distraction instead of escaping automatically.

pillars.title: Return Without Starting Over
pillars.body: Come back after a bad day without turning it into an identity crisis.

method.notePre: All in does not mean all output.
method.noteBold: It means no disconnection from the direction.

system.heading: One system for the life you are actually trying to build.
system.lede: You don't need five subscriptions and a spreadsheet. Direction, action and reflection live in one place.

tabs.title: Objectives & OKRs
tabs.body: Set a direction, break it into measurable outcomes, and review your progress instead of guessing at it.

tabs.title: Tasks & Calendar
tabs.body: One inbox, one agenda. What you commit to shows up next to the time you actually have.

tabs.title: Values & Dream Board
tabs.body: Define what matters, then pin the future it points to. Every habit and task traces back to the dream that started it.

tabs.title: Habits
tabs.body: Track streaks, intent and reflection. Habits that serve a direction, not habits for their own sake.

tabs.title: Finances
tabs.body: Accounts, budgets and net worth tracked alongside your goals, not in a separate app you forget to open.

tabs.title: Journal & Reflection
tabs.body: Morning intentions, evening reflections, and a searchable record, so your patterns stop hiding from you.

tabs.title: Learning

system.foot: Fewer subscriptions. Fewer disconnected systems. One direction.

how.heading: Start with one direction. Build from there.

items.q: Is Cherut just another productivity app?
items.a: No. Most productivity apps stop at a task list. Cherut connects your values, objectives and daily actions in one system, and gives you a structure for the days you don't feel like showing up.

items.q: Do I need to be disciplined to use Cherut?
items.a: No. This isn't about discipline or laziness. It's about missing structure.

items.q: Does All In All The Time mean working all the time?
items.a: No. All in does not mean all output. It means no disconnection from the direction.

items.q: Do I need to set up my entire life to get started?
items.a: No. You only need to choose the next direction, and build the minimum system that result requires.

items.q: What happens if I stop using it for a few days?
items.a: You review and pick back up, without starting over.

items.q: Is there a free plan or freemium version?
items.a: No free plan, no trial. Every level is a paid commitment to the direction you choose.

items.q: Does Cherut replace therapy or psychological treatment?
items.a: No. Cherut is a personal execution system. It is not therapy, medical care, or a substitute for professional mental health treatment.

finalCta.heading: You do not need another restart.
finalCta.body: The life you want will be built by the direction you choose, the actions you repeat, and your ability to return when the hard days come. Your intensity already exists. Now give it a structure.

manifesto: Motivation is not a strategy. Structure is.
Your obsession is not the problem. The absence of a system is.
Discipline runs out. A well-built structure does not need it to.
All in does not mean all output. It means never disconnecting from your direction.
A bad day is not a verdict on who you are. It is a day to review and return from.
Cherut (חירות) means freedom in Hebrew — not freedom from responsibility, freedom through it.
Every feature that does not serve your direction is noise, no matter how well it is designed.
We build for the days you do not feel like showing up, not just the days you do.

principles.body: Motivation is unreliable. A well-designed system works on the hard days too. We build for consistency, not inspiration bursts.

principles.body: The OKR framework, habit science and spaced reflection are not motivational fluff — they are engineering applied to human behaviour.

principles.title: Freedom through responsibility

principles.title: Quiet, not loud
principles.body: Streaks and progress exist to show you the truth, not to gamify it. No badges, no engagement tricks, no dark patterns.

hero.title: Set up your system in 30 minutes
hero.lead: A step-by-step guide to get ALL IN ALL THE TIME from day one.

gettingStartedPage.checklistHeading: Seven steps. Thirty minutes. One system.

steps.title: Complete your profile
steps.body: Upload a photo, set your timezone, choose notification settings and define your working hours for better task planning.

steps.title: Define your core values
steps.body: Navigate to Values and choose 3–5 principles that guide your decisions. Write a short description for each and rank them. These become your compass.

steps.title: Set up your life areas
steps.body: Create 4–6 life domains (Health, Career, Finance, Relationships…). Write a vision statement for each and set priority levels.

steps.title: Create your first OKRs
steps.body: Start with 1–2 objectives per life area. Write inspiring, qualitative objectives, then add 2–4 measurable key results with specific deadlines.

steps.title: Build success habits
steps.body: Create 3–5 keystone habits that support multiple objectives. Start small, set specific triggers, and link habits to your life areas and OKRs.

steps.title: Plan your first week
steps.body: Break key results into specific tasks. Schedule focused work blocks for the most important tasks. Plan habit execution times throughout the week.

steps.title: Set up tracking & reviews
steps.body: Configure your dashboard, schedule daily check-ins (5 min) and weekly reviews (30 min). Enable analytics to understand performance patterns.

tips.title: Start small, think big
tips.body: Consistent small wins beat ambitious failures. Build momentum early — the system compounds when you actually use it.

tips.title: Weekly reviews are non-negotiable
tips.body: Schedule 30 minutes every Sunday. Celebrate wins, analyze obstacles, adjust plans. This single habit is what separates drifters from executors.

tips.title: Connect everything to values
tips.body: When goals align with your core values, motivation becomes automatic. Always ask: why does this matter to me?

gettingStartedPage.ctaSub: The system is only as powerful as your commitment to using it.

hero.title: How can we help?
hero.lead: Guides, answers and everything you need to get the most out of Cherut.

articles.title: What is Cherut?
articles.body: Cherut is a personal operating system that connects your habits, tasks, OKRs, journal and vision board in one place. Start by setting up your Life Areas and creating your first Objective.

articles.title: Setting up your account
articles.body: After signing up, you land directly on the Dashboard — there's no mandatory onboarding flow, and no modules to turn on or off. Every module (Habits, Tasks, OKRs, Journal, Dream Board, Values, Life Areas, Finances) is already available in the sidebar; just use whichever ones make sense for you right now.

articles.title: Choosing your first module
articles.body: Not sure where to start? Most people begin with Habits or Tasks. Once you have a rhythm, add OKRs to give your daily actions a direction.

articles.title: Creating a habit
articles.body: Go to Habits → New Habit. Set a name, frequency (daily, weekdays, or custom days), and optionally link it to a Life Area or OKR.

articles.title: How streaks work
articles.body: A streak increments each day you complete a habit. Missing a day breaks the streak, but your completion history is always preserved.

articles.title: Archiving vs deleting
articles.body: Archive a habit to pause it without losing history. Delete only when you want to remove all records permanently.

articles.title: Creating a board
articles.body: Go to Tasks and click "New Board". Give it a name and optionally assign it to a Life Area. Boards have columns you can rename and reorder.

articles.title: Moving tasks between columns
articles.body: Drag a task card to any column, or open the task and change its status from the dropdown.

articles.title: Linking tasks to OKRs
articles.body: Inside any task, use the "Linked OKR" field to connect it to a Key Result. Progress is reflected in your OKR view.

articles.title: What are OKRs?
articles.body: OKRs (Objectives and Key Results) are a goal-setting framework. An Objective is an ambitious qualitative goal; Key Results are measurable outcomes that indicate you have reached it.

articles.title: Setting your first OKR
articles.body: Go to OKRs → New Objective. Write a clear, inspiring objective for the quarter. Then add 1–5 Key Results with numeric targets.

articles.title: Weekly check-ins
articles.body: Every week, open each Key Result and update the current value. Add a confidence score and a short note. Cherut tracks the trend over time.

articles.title: Changing your plan
articles.body: Self-service plan management is on the way. Until it ships, contact us to change or cancel your plan and we'll take care of it directly.

articles.title: Exporting your data
articles.body: Go to Settings → Data → Export. Your habits, tasks, OKRs, journal and all other data are exported as a single JSON file.

articles.title: Deleting your account
articles.body: Go to Settings → Account → Delete account. This permanently removes all your data. It cannot be undone. Export first if you want a copy.

hero.title: Your privacy is not a footnote.
hero.lead: Plain language. No surprises. Last updated May 2026.

privacyPolicyPage.notice: This is a plain-language summary of our privacy practices. It is designed to be readable, not exhaustive. For the full legal text, contact us at contact@hanielrolemberg.com

sections.title: What we collect
items: Your email address and name when you sign up.
Usage data: which features you use and when, to improve the product.
Content you create: habits, tasks, journal entries, OKRs. Stored encrypted.
Device and browser type for debugging and performance.

sections.title: What we don't do
items: We do not sell your data — ever. Not to advertisers, not to data brokers.
We do not show you ads. There are no ad networks in Cherut.
We do not use your journal, habits or goals to train AI models.
We do not share your personal data with third parties without your consent.

sections.title: How we store it
items: Data is stored on Firebase (Google Cloud) with encryption at rest and in transit.
Backups run daily and are retained for 30 days.
We use industry-standard TLS for all data in transit.
Access to production data is restricted to core team members.

sections.title: Your rights
items: Export: you can download all your data as JSON at any time from Settings.
Delete: you can permanently delete your account and all associated data.
Correction: you can update or correct any personal information you have provided.
Portability: your exported data is in open formats, not locked in.

sections.title: Contact
items: Questions about this policy? Email us at contact@hanielrolemberg.com
We aim to respond to all privacy inquiries within 5 business days.
For urgent data deletion requests, include "URGENT" in your subject line.
